questions.question: Which musical instruments typically accompany the Gaur dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhol, Harmonium, and Manjira**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gaur dance** is one of the most prominent folk dances of the **Bison-Horn Maria** tribes, who primarily reside in the **Bastar** region of **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• The dance is traditionally performed during festive occasions and as a tribute to the spirit of the hunt, specifically mimicking the majestic movements of the **Indian Bison** (Gaur).
 
• The **Dhol** (a large double-headed drum) is the central instrument used to provide a powerful rhythmic pulse that dictates the pace and energy of the dancers.
 
• The **Manjira** (small brass cymbals) provides a sharp, metallic rhythmic accompaniment that complements the deep beats of the drum.
 
• The **Harmonium** is frequently used in contemporary and staged folk performances to provide a melodic foundation for the traditional songs that accompany the **Gaur dance**.
 
• Male dancers typically wear a striking headdress made of **bison horns**, decorated with **peacock feathers** and **cowrie shells**, while women carry **Tirududi** (iron rattles) to add to the soundscape.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sitar and Tabla**:

 
 
• The **Sitar** is a plucked string instrument used in **Hindustani classical music**.
 
• The **Tabla** consists of a pair of hand drums and is the primary percussion in **North Indian** classical traditions.
 
 
 
• **Mridangam**:
 
 
• This is a primary percussion instrument of **Carnatic music** from South India, known for its distinct barrel shape and complex tonal variations.
 
 
 
• **Shehnai**:
 
 
• A double-reed oboe-like instrument associated with **auspicious events** and weddings, popularized globally by **Ustad Bismillah Khan**.
 
 
 
• **Bastar Cultural Heritage**:
 
 
• The **Muria** and **Maria** tribes possess a rich heritage of **ethno-musicology**, often using instruments crafted from local wood, bamboo, and animal hide.
 
• The **Gaur dance** is considered a symbol of tribal strength and communal harmony within the **Gond** cultural complex.

questions.question: According to Natyasastra, musical instruments are classified into how many categories?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Natyasastra**, an ancient Indian treatise on performing arts attributed to the sage **Bharata Muni**, provides the earliest systematic classification of musical instruments, categorizing them into **four** distinct groups.
 
• These four categories are collectively referred to as **Atodya** or **Vadya**, based on the physical characteristics of the instrument and the method of sound production.
 
• The first category is **Tata Vadya**, which refers to **stringed instruments** or chordophones, where sound is produced by the vibration of strings.
 
• The second category is **Sushira Vadya**, encompassing **wind instruments** or aerophones, where sound is generated by the passage of air through a hollow column.
 
• The third category is **Avanaddha Vadya**, denoting **percussion instruments** or membranophones, which consist of a hollow vessel covered with a **stretched skin** or membrane.
 
• The fourth category is **Ghana Vadya**, which includes **solid instruments** or idiophones made of metal or wood that produce sound by striking and do not require tuning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Detailed Characteristics of the Four Categories:
 
 
• **Tata Vadya**: These instruments are played by plucking, bowing, or striking strings. Key examples mentioned in historical texts include the **Veena**, **Ektara**, and later developments like the **Sitar** and **Sarod**.
 
• **Sushira Vadya**: These are characterized by air pressure. The **Venu** (flute) and **Shankha** (conch) are classic examples. The pitch is controlled by opening or closing finger holes.
 
• **Avanaddha Vadya**: Primarily used for maintaining **Tala** (rhythm), these include the **Mridangam**, **Tabla**, **Dholak**, and **Pakhawaj**. They are essential for both Carnatic and Hindustani classical music.
 
• **Ghana Vadya**: These are non-membranous percussion instruments. Examples include **Manjira** (cymbals), **Karthal**, and **Ghatam** (clay pot). They are typically used to keep time during performances.
 
 
 
• The **Natyasastra** is believed to have been composed between **200 BCE and 200 CE** and serves as the foundational text for **Indian Classical Music**, dance, and drama.

questions.question: The Sari Shop (Novel) is written by which of the following authors?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rupa Bajwa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Sari Shop** is the debut novel of Indian author **Rupa Bajwa**, first published in **2004**.
 
• The story is set in the city of **Amritsar**, Punjab, and centers on the life of **Ramchand**, a shop assistant working at a high-end clothing store called **Seva Ram and Sons**.
 
• The narrative masterfully explores the **social hierarchy** and **class divide** in modern India by contrasting the mundane, restricted life of the shop assistants with the opulent lifestyles of their wealthy clientele.
 
• The novel received critical acclaim for its poignant portrayal of **urban poverty**, **aspiration**, and the harsh realities faced by the working class in provincial India.
 
• For this work, **Rupa Bajwa** was awarded the **Commonwealth Writers Prize** for Best First Book (Eurasia) in **2005**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rupa Bajwa**:

 
 
• She is an **Amritsar-based** novelist who achieved international fame with her first book.
 
• In **2006**, she was honored with the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in English for **The Sari Shop**.
 
 
 
• **R.K. Narayan**:
 
 
• One of the most famous early Indian novelists in English, best known for creating the fictional town of **Malgudi** and writing **The Guide** and **Swami and Friends**.
 
 
 
• **Shashi Tharoor**:
 
 
• A prominent Indian politician and author of several acclaimed works including **The Great Indian Novel**, **An Era of Darkness**, and **Show Business**.
 
 
 
• **Anjali Banerjee**:
 
 
• An Indian-American author known for novels such as **Maya Running**, **Haunting Jasmine**, and **Seaglass Summer**.

questions.question: Air Quality Index (AQI) "Moderate" category indicates:

options.text: Air quality may cause health effects for sensitive groups.
Air quality is hazardous to all.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Air quality may cause health effects for sensitive groups**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Air Quality Index (AQI)** is a standardized system used to report daily air quality and communicate the associated **health risks** to the public.
 
• In the **Moderate** category, which typically corresponds to an index range of **101 to 200** on the **National Air Quality Index (NAQI)** scale in India, air quality is considered acceptable for the general population.
 
• However, for individuals belonging to **sensitive groups**—such as children, the elderly, and those with pre-existing **respiratory diseases** like asthma or **cardiovascular conditions**—this level of pollution can trigger **breathing discomfort**.
 
• The **Moderate** level indicates that while the air is not yet hazardous to all, there is a sufficient concentration of pollutants like **PM2.5** or **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2)** to affect vulnerable biological systems.
 
• The primary health implication in this category is the aggravation of symptoms in patients with **lung and heart ailments**, requiring them to limit heavy outdoor exertion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **AQI** structure is divided into six distinct categories, each defined by a specific color code and health advisory:

 
 
• **Good (0–50)**: Minimal impact; the air quality is considered **excellent** and poses little to no health risk.
 
• **Satisfactory (51–100)**: May cause minor breathing discomfort to sensitive people.
 
• **Poor (201–300)**: Likely to cause breathing discomfort to most people on prolonged exposure.
 
• **Very Poor (301–400)**: May lead to **respiratory illness** on prolonged exposure and has a more pronounced effect on people with lung and heart diseases.
 
• **Severe (401–500)**: Air quality is **hazardous**; it affects healthy people and seriously impacts those with existing diseases, even with light physical activity.
 
 
 
• The calculation of **AQI** in India considers eight major pollutants: **PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3,** and **Pb** (Lead).

questions.question: A satellite in geostationary orbit remains fixed above a point on Earth's equator. The satellite's orbital radius is about 42,200 km. Calculate the orbital period of the satellite in hours.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**24 hr**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **geostationary satellite** is a satellite that circles the Earth in an orbit such that it remains exactly above a fixed point on the **equator** at all times.
 
• For a satellite to appear stationary relative to the Earth, its **angular velocity** must be equal to the **Earth's rotation** angular velocity around its own axis.
 
• The **orbital period** of a geostationary satellite is precisely one **sidereal day**, which is approximately **23 hours, 56 minutes, and 4 seconds**. In the context of most general physics problems and competitive exams, this is rounded to **24 hr**.
 
• At an **orbital radius** of approximately **42,200 km** (which corresponds to an altitude of about **35,786 km** above the Earth's surface), the **centripetal force** required for the circular motion is perfectly balanced by the Earth's **gravitational pull**.
 
• Since the satellite moves from **west to east** (prograde motion) with the same period as the Earth, its **relative velocity** with respect to any fixed observer on the ground is zero.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kepler's Third Law**:

 
 
• The law states that the square of the **orbital period (T)** is directly proportional to the cube of the **semi-major axis (r)** of its orbit, expressed as **T² ∝ r³**.
 
• For the Earth, when **r** is roughly **42,200 km**, **T** calculates to approximately **86,164 seconds**.
 
 
 
• **Orbital Velocity**:
 
 
• A satellite in this orbit travels at a constant **orbital speed** of approximately **3.07 km/s** to maintain its position.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• This specific orbital belt is often called the **Clarke Belt**, named after the scientist and writer **Arthur C. Clarke**, who first proposed the use of **geostationary orbits** for worldwide **telecommunications** relays.
 
 
 
• **Common Uses**:
 
 
• **Geostationary satellites** are primary tools for **weather forecasting**, **satellite television (DTH)**, and **radio broadcasting** because they provide continuous coverage of a specific geographic area.

questions.question: Which strait does Chabahar Port bypass, providing easier access to global trade routes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Strait of Hormuz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chabahar Port** is located in the **Sistan-Baluchestan province** on the southeastern coast of **Iran**, along the **Gulf of Oman**.
 
• The port's strategic location allows maritime trade to bypass the **Strait of Hormuz**, which is a narrow and often congested waterway that serves as the only sea passage from the **Persian Gulf** to the open ocean.
 
• By operating outside the **Strait of Hormuz**, Chabahar reduces the dependency of international shipping on this sensitive chokepoint, through which approximately **one-fifth** of the world's total oil consumption passes daily.
 
• It serves as a critical transit hub for **India** to access **Afghanistan** and **Central Asian** landlocked republics, effectively bypassing the land routes through **Pakistan**.
 
• The port is a key component of the **International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC)**, aimed at reducing freight costs and transit time between **India**, **Iran**, and **Russia**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Strait of Malacca**

 
 
• Located between the **Malay Peninsula** and the Indonesian island of **Sumatra**.
 
• It is the main shipping channel between the **Indian Ocean** and the **Pacific Ocean**.
 
 
 
• **Strait of Gibraltar**
 
 
• A narrow strait that connects the **Atlantic Ocean** to the **Mediterranean Sea**.
 
• It separates the continents of **Europe** (Spain) and **Africa** (Morocco).
 
 
 
• **Bab el-Mandeb Strait**
 
 
• Located between **Yemen** on the Arabian Peninsula and **Djibouti** and **Eritrea** in the Horn of Africa.
 
• It connects the **Red Sea** to the **Gulf of Aden** and the **Arabian Sea**.
 
 
 
• **Chabahar Port Development**
 
 
• The port consists of two separate terminals: **Shahid Beheshti** and **Shahid Kalantari**.
 
• India's involvement is primarily focused on the development of the **Shahid Beheshti** terminal through **India Ports Global Limited (IPGL)**.

questions.question: Financial sector reforms post-1991 included:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All of these**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The financial sector reforms post-**1991**, based on the **Narasimham Committee** recommendations, allowed the **entry of private sector banks** to foster competition and improve efficiency in the banking system, leading to the birth of institutions like **HDFC Bank** and **ICICI Bank**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Strengthening capital markets** was achieved by granting statutory powers to the **Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)** in **1992**, which helped regulate the stock exchanges, protect investors, and promote a transparent trading environment. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The **deregulation of interest rates** was a major reform where the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** allowed commercial banks to determine their own **lending and deposit rates** based on market forces, shifting away from a centrally controlled administered interest rate regime. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• These reforms collectively aimed at **liberalization**, **privatization**, and **globalization** of the Indian economy to integrate it with the global financial system. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narasimham Committee (1991)**:

 
 
• Recommended the reduction of the **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** and **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** to increase the availability of funds for the private sector.
 
• Introduced **Prudential Norms** and **Asset Classification** to ensure banks maintain a healthy balance sheet and **Capital Adequacy Ratio**.
 
 
 
• **Market Infrastructure**:
 
 
• The establishment of the **National Stock Exchange (NSE)** in **1992** introduced **screen-based trading**, replacing the traditional floor-based system.
 
• **Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs)** were permitted to invest in Indian debt and equity markets starting in **1992-93**.

questions.question: Who was honored with the 'Fred Darrington Award for Excellence in Art and Culture' in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sudarshan Pattnaik**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sudarshan Pattnaik**, the world-renowned Indian **sand artist** hailing from **Puri, Odisha**, was honored with the prestigious **Fred Darrington Award for Excellence in Art and Culture**.
 
• The honor was bestowed upon him at the **21st International Sand Sculpting Festival** held at **Revere Beach** in **Boston, USA**, highlighting his global influence in the realm of sculpture.
 
• The **Fred Darrington Award** is named after the pioneer of sand sculpting at Revere Beach, who is credited with initiating the craft in the **late 19th century**; it recognizes artists who demonstrate exceptional skill and creative mastery.
 
• Pattnaik is celebrated for his unique **3D sand art** style and his commitment to using the medium for **social activism**, covering themes such as **World Peace**, **Global Warming**, and **Environmental Protection**.
 
• With over **27 international awards** to his credit, Pattnaik has represented India in more than **65 international championships** across countries like **Italy**, **Russia**, and **Japan**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sudarshan Pattnaik’s Career Highlights**:

 
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Shri**, India’s fourth-highest civilian award, in **2014** for his unparalleled contributions to the field of arts.
 
• He achieved a **Guinness World Record** in **2017** for building the world’s tallest sandcastle, which stood at a height of **14.84 meters** (approximately 48 feet).
 
• Pattnaik established the **Sudarshan Sand Art Institute** in Puri to provide formal training to aspiring sand artists, fostering the next generation of sculptors.
 
 
 
• **Revere Beach International Sand Sculpting Festival**:
 
 
• Established as a major event in **Massachusetts**, it is considered one of the largest and most competitive sand art festivals in the **Western Hemisphere**.
 
• The festival attracts approximately **1 million visitors** annually and features master sculptors from around the globe competing for top honors.

questions.question: Which river is known as the 'Dakshina Ganga'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Godavari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Godavari** is the largest **Peninsular river** system in India, often referred to as the **Dakshina Ganga** (Ganges of the South) due to its extensive length and the vast area it covers.
 
• It originates from the **Trimbakeshwar** in the **Nashik** district of **Maharashtra**, situated in the **Western Ghats** at an elevation of about 1,067 meters.
 
• The river flows for a total length of approximately **1,465 kilometers**, traversing through the states of **Maharashtra**, **Telangana**, and **Andhra Pradesh** before draining into the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• Its drainage basin is the second largest in India after the **Ganga**, covering about **3,12,812 square kilometers**, which is nearly 9.5 percent of the total geographical area of the country.
 
• The river is also known as **Vridha Ganga** (Old Ganga) because of its ancient geological origin and its religious significance in **Hinduism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Krishna**

 
 
• The **Krishna River** is the second-largest eastward-flowing peninsular river, originating near **Mahabaleshwar** in **Maharashtra**.
 
• Its major tributaries include the **Tungabhadra**, **Koyna**, **Ghataprabha**, **Musl**, and **Bhima**.
 
 
 
• **Cauvery**
 
 
• Originating from the **Brahmagiri range** of the **Western Ghats** in **Karnataka**, it is often called the **Dakshin Bharat ki Ganga**.
 
• It is a **perennial river** due to receiving rainfall from both the **Southwest** and **Northeast monsoons**.
 
 
 
• **Narmada**
 
 
• The **Narmada** is a major west-flowing river that originates from the **Amarkantak Plateau** in **Madhya Pradesh**.
 
• It flows through a **rift valley** formed by faulting between the **Vindhya** and **Satpura** ranges.

questions.question: Which region is historically known as the "Manchester of India" for its cotton textile industry?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ahmedabad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ahmedabad**, located in **Gujarat** on the banks of the **Sabarmati River**, is historically renowned as the **Manchester of India** due to its massive cotton textile industry.
 
• The city earned this moniker because its textile development mirrored that of **Manchester** in **England**, which was the global center of the cotton industry during the **Industrial Revolution**.
 
• The **first cotton textile mill** in Ahmedabad was established in **1861** by **Shri Ranchhodlal Chhotalal**, marking the beginning of an industrial era for the city.
 
• The growth of the industry was supported by the proximity of **cotton-growing regions** in Gujarat and Maharashtra, ensuring a steady supply of raw materials.
 
• The **humid climate** of the region is naturally suited for **spinning** and **weaving**, as it prevents the cotton thread from breaking easily during processing.
 
• Strategic location with access to **Kandla Port** and a well-developed **railway network** facilitated the export of finished goods and the import of machinery.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mumbai-Pune Region**:

 
 
• **Mumbai** was traditionally known as the **Cottonopolis of India** because the first successful mechanized textile mill was established here in **1854** by **Cowasji Nanabhoy Davar**.
 
 
 
• **Kanpur**:
 
 
• Located in **Uttar Pradesh**, Kanpur is often referred to as the **Manchester of North India** due to its significant concentration of textile and leather industries.
 
 
 
• **Coimbatore**:
 
 
• Situated in **Tamil Nadu**, this city is called the **Manchester of South India** because it houses over 1,000 textile mills and contributes significantly to India's cotton exports.
 
 
 
• **Textile Industry Significance**:
 
 
• It is the **second-largest employment generator** in India after agriculture and accounts for a substantial portion of the country's **Industrial Production** and **GDP**.

questions.question: Which scheme specifically supports MSMEs for technology upgradation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS)** was launched by the **Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MoMSME)** to facilitate **technology upgradation** by providing upfront capital subsidies.
 
• The scheme aims at helping **MSMEs** modernize their **production techniques** and equipment to improve product quality and reduce production costs.
 
• Under this scheme, a **15 percent capital subsidy** is provided to eligible MSMEs on institutional finance (bank loans) availed by them for the induction of well-established and improved technology.
 
• The maximum limit of the loan eligible for subsidy under the current guidelines is **Rs. 1 crore**, meaning the maximum subsidy amount an enterprise can receive is capped at **Rs. 15 lakh**.
 
• Implementation is carried out through **Nodal Agencies** such as the **Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)**, **NABARD**, and designated public sector banks.
 
• It covers a wide range of industries including **food processing**, **textiles**, **leather**, **pharmaceuticals**, and **electronic equipment**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)**:

 
 
• A credit-linked subsidy program aimed at **generating self-employment** opportunities through the establishment of **micro-enterprises**.
 
• It is implemented by the **Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)** at the national level.
 
 
 
• **Make in India Scheme**:
 
 
• Launched in **September 2014**, this initiative focuses on transforming India into a global **manufacturing hub** by encouraging domestic and foreign investment.
 
• It targets **25 key sectors** including automobiles, chemicals, and IT.
 
 
 
• **Atal Innovation Mission (AIM)**:
 
 
• A flagship initiative by **NITI Aayog** to promote a culture of **innovation** and **entrepreneurship**.
 
• It manages programs like **Atal Tinkering Labs (ATLs)** and **Atal Incubation Centres (AICs)**.

questions.question: Which language was adopted by Jainism as its sacred language in ancient India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prakrit**__.

questions.question: In the context of the Sangam age, all the three 'Sangams' took place under the patronage of ____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandya kings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Sangam** refers to an academy or assembly of **Tamil poets** and scholars that flourished under the royal patronage of the **Pandya kings** of **Madurai**.
 
• According to **Tamil legends**, there were three Sangams (assemblies) held in **Ancient South India**, spanning thousands of years, collectively referred to as **Muchchangam**.
 
• The **First Sangam** (Mudal Sangam) is believed to have been held at **Thenmadurai** (Old Madurai). It was reportedly attended by gods and legendary sages like **Agastya**; however, no literary works from this period are available today.
 
• The **Second Sangam** (Idai Sangam) was held at **Kapatapuram**. The only surviving literary work from this assembly is the **Tolkappiyam**, which is a comprehensive treatise on **Tamil grammar** and poetics.
 
• The **Third Sangam** (Kadai Sangam) was situated at the modern city of **Madurai**. Most of the surviving **Sangam literature**, including the **Ettutogai** (Eight Anthologies) and the **Pattupattu** (Ten Idylls), belongs to this period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangam Dynasties**:

 
 
• While the **Pandya kings** were the specific patrons of the Sangams, the literature produced describes the **Muventar** (Three Crowned Kings): the **Cheras**, **Cholas**, and **Pandyas**.
 
 
 
• **Major Literary Works**:
 
 
• **Tolkappiyam**: Authored by **Tolkappiyar**, it is the oldest extant Tamil work, providing insights into the social and linguistic structure of the **Sangam Age**.
 
• **Pathinenkilkanakku**: A collection of eighteen lower ethical works, including the famous **Tirukkural** by **Thiruvalluvar**, which focuses on ethics and philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Social Structure**: The Sangam society was classified based on five ecological zones or **Thinai**, namely **Kurinji** (hilly), **Mullai** (pastoral), **Marutham** (agricultural), **Neithal** (coastal), and **Palai** (desert).

questions.question:
Which of the following region is densely populated in India?

I. The Brahmaputra Plains II. The Ganga Plains
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Brahmaputra Plains**, primarily located in **Assam**, represent a significant physiographic division characterized by a level topography and rich **alluvial deposits**. While the surrounding northeastern hills are sparsely populated, the valley floor supports high population densities due to intensive **rice cultivation** and **tea plantations**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• The **Ganga Plains** constitute the largest part of the **Great Northern Plains** of India, stretching across states like **Haryana**, **Delhi**, **Uttar Pradesh**, **Bihar**, and **West Bengal**. This region is one of the most **densely populated** tracts in the world because of its extremely **fertile soil**, perennial water supply from the **Ganga river system**, and favorable climate for year-round agriculture. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Factors Influencing High Population Density:**

 
 
• **Topography:** The **flat terrain** of these plains facilitates the construction of massive **transportation networks** (roads and railways) and the establishment of large **industrial hubs**.
 
• **Agriculture:** The deposition of **Khadar** (new alluvium) and **Bhangar** (old alluvium) makes these plains the **granary of India**, supporting high food security for a large population.
 
• **Water Availability:** The presence of **Himalayan rivers** ensures a constant supply of water for **irrigation**, domestic use, and industrial processes.
 
• **Urbanization:** Historical centers and modern **megacities** like **Kolkata**, **Patna**, and **Kanpur** are situated in these plains, acting as magnets for migration.
 
 
 
• **Demographic Contrast:** In contrast to these plains, the **Himalayan mountains** and the **Thar Desert** exhibit low population density due to **rugged terrain**, extreme climatic conditions, and limited **arable land**.
